Summary of Transit Gaps
● The existing services were limited in coverage of the City, especially in areas with newer
neighborhoods or new employers.
● The network covered a lot of key destinations, including the downtown area, shopping
areas, and social service providers. However, some new employers and new facilities were
not accessible by transit.
● The radial fixed-route network had many one-way loops and circuitous patterns, resulting in
long journey times. Schedules based on run times and driver shifts resulted in some long
and inconvenient transfers. These features limited the service's usefulness and impacted
rider experiences.
● Preliminary expansion of the On-Demand service to citywide on Saturdays indicated a
desire for access to other parts of the City beyond the existing network.
● Some routes, particularly routes 4 and 9, were very efficient. However, the highest
productivity routes were not necessarily those with the highest ridership, indicating a
potential mismatch in the allocation of fixed-route service with ridership demand.

5. SAM Reimagine Plan Summary
The City Council approved the recommendations on June 13, 2024. Once the plan was approved,
the team moved forward with the implementation of the recommendations. During June, July,
August, and September, the team finalized the service plan, including the bus stops, continued to
engage and inform the community about the changes, and implemented new infrastructure for the
service changes. The weekday expansion of SAM On Demand was launched on August 8, 2024,
and the changes to the fixed-route buses were implemented on September 16, 2024.

Summary of Implemented SAM Reimagined Plan
● Transit access expanded to 100% of Sioux Falls.
● Fixed-route network reduced to nine direct and frequent routes. Minimization of loops and
circuitous routing.
● New clock-facing schedules for easier travel and shorter transfer times.
● On-demand coverage expanded to citywide on weekdays, matching fixed-route hours.
● SAM Transit App expanded to facilitate trip planning, bus tracking, and intermodal journeys.
Retainment of options to make trip requests by phone or in person, as needed.
● Saturday service hours expanded to 615 PM (previously 3 PM.
● No reduction to paratransit service coverage.

6. Preliminary Post-Launch Analysis
Figure 28 shows the ridership and productivity for each route during the entire month of October.
The average productivity of the network was 12 boardings per hour. While initial average
productivity is a bit lower than before the changes, the fluctuation by route is much smaller,
indicating that the route frequencies and service hours (which contribute to the monthly revenue
hours) are well matched to the routeʼs ridership demand. As ridership continues to grow, the
productivity of the routes will also increase.

Next Steps
● Continue marketing the service and executing rider education outreach efforts to grow
ridership.
● Continuously monitor ridership and travel patterns to determine opportunities to expand
service including, areas or times of day/days of the week to add fixed route frequency,
route extensions, or expanding SAM On Demand capacity at particular times of
day/days of the week.
● Continuously monitor ridership and travel patterns on fixed-route service to determine
opportunities to switch service delivery to SAM On Demand, including entire fixed
routes, route segments or times of day/days of the week where areas may be better
served by SAM On Demand.
● Evaluate ridership patterns and meet with stakeholders and riders to understand priority
areas for additional infrastructure improvements (e.g., shelters, seating at bus stops,
etc.).
● Work with the operating team to continue to improve efficiencies and the rider
experience in response to driver, rider, and city needs.
